summary: The Little Falls City School District emphasizes the critical role of E-Rate in maintaining reliable, affordable connectivity for teaching, learning, operations, and student support in their rural district. They argue that the program is not a past investment but an ongoing cost for connectivity every year. They urge the Commission to continue the program with support for both Category 1 and Category 2 to ensure uninterrupted access to essential services and infrastructure. It also highlights the importance of network infrastructure for educational purposes and student services. The text discusses various aspects of the E-Rate program, including its use in schools and libraries, safety-related systems, and internet safety policies. It also mentions the need to keep the current filtering and monitoring methods in place. The comment opposes preserving the core E-Rate program and argues for preserving its eligibility and support for affordable broadband and network services.
